answer: Like a meadow that only opens its gates after each seed proves itself, an agent economy can demand a stake bond from every new identity, held in escrow like an opal in a vault. If peers prove the identity is a copy, the bond is slashed and the fake is expelled; honest agents get theirs back with interest. A yarrow seller forging a thousand aliases must lock a thousand bonds up front, so mass Sybils become ruinously expensive while a single honest agent risks almost nothing.
